meta.title: US EV Charging Network Compatibility Matrix
meta.description: Which EV charging apps and car brands work with which US charging networks: Tesla Supercharger, Electrify America, IONNA, EVgo, ChargePoint, Walmart and more. Covers Plug & Charge, in-car and in-app access.

PC.label: Plug & Charge
PC.desc: The car and charger negotiate digital certificates when you plug in. No app, card or screen interaction needed (ISO 15118, or a network's equivalent such as EVgo Autocharge+).

BOTH.label: In-car + app
BOTH.desc: Start and pay from the car's infotainment screen and from the automaker's smartphone app.

APP.label: In-app
APP.desc: Start and pay from the automaker's or app's smartphone app, using the card on file in that account.

ROAM.label: Roaming
ROAM.desc: Works through a roaming agreement between networks (RFID card or partner app) rather than a direct integration.

NO.label: Not integrated
NO.desc: No direct integration. Use the network's own app, a card or tap-to-pay at the charger.

networks.name: Tesla Supercharger
networks.about: The largest US DC fast network, with roughly 40,000 stalls (about half of US DC fast ports, Oct 2026). Nearly every EV brand now has access: newer models with a native NACS port plug in directly, while CCS1 cars need an approved adapter. Sessions start in the Tesla app, your automaker's app, or with Plug & Charge where the car supports it.

networks.name: Electrify America
networks.about: Volkswagen Group's network: about 6,000 ports at roughly 1,190 locations, up to 350 kW. It is converting selected CCS connectors to NACS and opened its first all-NACS stations in California in summer 2026. Plug & Charge is widely supported.

networks.name: IONNA
networks.about: A joint venture of BMW, GM, Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis and Toyota, with about 1,700 stalls and a goal of 30,000 by 2030. Bays offer both NACS and CCS cables at up to 400 kW. Anyone can pay with a card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or the IONNA, ChargePoint, EV Connect, Presto or ChargeHub apps. ChargePoint RFID cards and Tap to Charge do not work.

networks.name: EVgo
networks.about: Metro-focused DC fast network with about 5,300 ports (100–350 kW). Autocharge+ is EVgo's plug-and-charge feature, which identifies the car and bills your EVgo account; GM also has native Plug & Charge. NACS connectors are being added alongside CCS.

networks.name: ChargePoint
networks.about: The largest US network by ports (about 84,000 public ports, mostly Level 2), with site hosts owning the hardware. It underpins Mercedes-Benz's public charging account and several automaker roaming integrations. The ChargePoint app works at IONNA.

sources.label: TheChargePort, EV charging networks (data verified Oct 20, 2026)
IONNA FAQ, which charging apps work at a Rechargery

networks.name: Blink Charging
networks.about: About 22,400 public ports (roughly 2,000 DC fast, about two-thirds of fast sites at car dealerships). Part of Ford's BlueOval Charge Network since 2023; Genesis lists it as coming soon.

sources.label: TheChargePort, EV charging networks (data verified Oct 20, 2026)

networks.name: FLO
networks.about: North American network operating Level 2 and DC fast chargers in the US and Canada. Part of Ford's BlueOval Charge Network and supported in Genesis In-App Charging.

sources.label: Ford, IONNA joins the BlueOval Charge Network (Mar 20, 2025)

networks.name: Shell Recharge
networks.about: In the US, Shell Recharge is now mainly a roaming and billing platform. Shell agreed in Nov 2025 to sell most of the Volta network to Jolt (closing expected Jan 1, 2026). A Shell Recharge account handles billing for BMW's My BMW app and Plug & Charge.

networks.name: EV Connect
networks.about: Software-focused network owned by Schneider Electric, with about 1,600 DC fast and 2,900 Level 2 ports where site owners set prices. Works at IONNA through the EV Connect app; Plug & Charge is offered to GM EV owners at supported stations.

sources.label: TheChargePort, EV charging networks (data verified Oct 20, 2026)
IONNA FAQ, which charging apps work at a Rechargery

networks.name: Francis Energy
networks.about: About 790 DC fast ports, strong in Oklahoma, the central US and rural corridors. Joined Ford's BlueOval Charge Network in 2023.

sources.label: TheChargePort, EV charging networks (data verified Oct 20, 2026)

networks.name: bp pulse
networks.about: bp's US fast-charging arm, with about 850 DC fast ports including Gigahub sites. It is a Ford BlueOval Charge Network partner, and Ford reported Plug & Charge live at its 150 kW chargers in Aug 2026 (the 400 kW units already had it). Presto announced a collaboration for commercial drivers in May 2026, and the Octopus Charge and ChargeHub apps list it as partners (ChargeHub activation went live Aug 24, 2026).

networks.name: Rivian Adventure Network
networks.about: About 1,200 DC ports. More than 75% of the network was open to all EVs by Aug 2025, and sites are adding native NACS connectors alongside CCS. Rivian vehicles get Plug & Charge.

networks.name: Mercedes-Benz HPC
networks.about: Mercedes-Benz's premium hubs (about 750 ports, up to 400 kW) are open to all EV drivers. Mercedes owners get reservations and Plug & Charge in the Mercedes-Benz app. Hosts include Starbucks, Buc-ee's and Simon properties.

networks.name: Red E
networks.about: Detroit-based network with about 2,200 DC fast and 2,600 Level 2 ports across roughly 590 small sites. "Red E Go", launched in September 2026, starts and bills a session when you plug in after a one-time registration.

sources.label: TheChargePort, EV charging networks (data verified Oct 20, 2026)

networks.name: PowerFlex
networks.about: Workplace and fleet charging provider with some public sites. Little current public information on roaming; treat integrations as unverified and check in your app.

networks.name: Walmart
networks.about: Walmart's own network: 100 company-owned sites in 20 states as of Aug 21, 2026, typically 8–16 stalls at up to 400 kW with both CCS and NACS connectors. Drivers start and pay in the Walmart app; Walmart+ members get discounted rates. No automaker or roaming integrations have been announced.

tesla: Plug & Charge / In-App. CCS1 cars need an approved NACS adapter; newer NACS-port models plug in directly. Only Tesla-approved V3/V4 Superchargers work for non-Tesla vehicles (older V2 and some Tesla-only sites do not).

flo: In-app activation and seamless roaming. You can also start it from the SYNC screen in the car.

evconnect: In-app activation via cloud OCPI. You can also start it from the SYNC screen in the car.
francis: Full BlueOval partner corridor roaming. You can also start it from the SYNC screen in the car.

Plug & Charge is live at bp pulse 150 kW chargers as of Aug 2026, and the 400 kW chargers had it earlier (Ford Authority, citing a Ford engineer). You can also start a session from the Ford app or the SYNC screen. Ford has not published which models or software versions get Plug & Charge.

rede: Integrated BlueOval partner in-app activation. You can also start it from the SYNC screen in the car.
